siteLines: Half the goods traded in Qaracaravansarai are only passing through.
Members of Qaracaravansarai's merchant guild do most of the buying and selling that matters.
Qaracaravansarai's warehouses fill after the harvest and empty through the year as the town trades out of them.
In Qaracaravansarai the law keeps a building of its own.
Qaracaravansarai sets its days by the cathedral bells: the feasts, the burials and the hours of work all follow them.

legitimacyBanner.sentence: Terraium neither backs the Merchant Guild Council nor opposes it. Routine orders are obeyed; a hard decision would find nobody willing to carry it.

legitimacyLens.sentence: Terraium is doing well and gives the Merchant Guild Council the credit. While the money keeps coming, nobody looks hard at how it governs.

stabilityHeader.sentence: A trader with a complaint at Terraium takes it to Merchant Guild Council.

stabilityLens.sentence: Terraium is still living with its recent quarrel, and the hall is run the way it is because of who won it.

operationReading.sentence: The customs at Terraium keep proper books, and a good share of goods goes around them anyway.

successionRisk.sentence: Merchant Guild Council outweighs everyone at Terraium who wants its place, and the whole city knows who they are. Merchant Guild Council holds on, but has to watch them.

successionHold.sentence: Terraium neither backs the Merchant Guild Council nor moves against it, and the Merchant Guild Council governs on its own strength alone.

rulingStructure.sentence: The people who run Terraium are also the people it owes money to, and they do not keep the two apart.

governingTitle.sentence: Terraium calls its hall the Merchant Guild Council in public and something shorter everywhere else.
